written.followUp: What happens to an operating system when a computer is started from its hard disk?

rubric.why: The answer should identify the source of the operating system during startup.
rubric.description: States that the operating system is loaded from the hard disk.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the hard disk as the source.

rubric.why: The answer should identify where the operating system is loaded for use.
rubric.description: States that the operating system is loaded into RAM (main memory).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming RAM or main memory as the destination.

written.text: Define router.
modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that connects two or more networks and forwards data packets between them, using IP addresses to direct the packets.
written.followUp: Define a switch in a computer network.

rubric.why: Checks the router’s role in connecting networks.
rubric.description: States that a router connects two or more networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying that it connects networks.

rubric.why: Checks how a router directs network traffic.
rubric.description: States that it forwards data packets between networks, typically using IP addresses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing packet forwarding or IP-based routing.

written.text: What is meant by Candid Solution?
modelAnswer: A candid solution is a clear and straightforward solution to a problem.

written.followUp: What is meant by an unambiguous solution?

rubric.why: Identifies the clear and straightforward nature of a candid solution.
rubric.description: States that a candid solution is clear or straightforward.

rubric.why: Shows that a candid solution cannot be interpreted in different ways.
rubric.description: States that its meaning is definite and not open to confusion.

written.text: What is prototype?
modelAnswer: A prototype is a preliminary model of a system or product.

written.followUp: Why might a developer create a prototype before building the final system?

rubric.why: Award for identifying a prototype as an early version or model.
rubric.description: A prototype is a preliminary model of a system or product.

rubric.why: Award for explaining why a prototype is made.
rubric.description: It is used to test or evaluate the design and obtain feedback before the final system is developed.

written.text: Describe the main characteristics of a computer as a system, including its objectives, components, and interactions among these components.

Interface components include input devices such as the keyboard and mouse, and output devices such as monitors and printers.

The motherboard interconnects components, while the system bus transmits data between the CPU and other components.

written.text: Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).
modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all devices share a single communication line called a bus.
If the main cable fails, the whole network goes down.
In a star topology, each node communicates with the others via a central switch or hub.
The hub works as a data flow repeater.
In a ring topology, each device is connected in a circular pathway with other devices.
Data travels in one direction, passing through each device; if one connection fails, the whole network is affected.
In a mesh topology, each device is connected to every other device.
This provides high redundancy and reliability because data can be rerouted through other links.
written.followUp: What are the advantages of using a star topology in a network?

rubric.description: Explains bus topology.
rubric.why: Describing the bus arrangement and its key weakness shows understanding of this topology.
rubric.how: State that devices share one bus cable and that its failure can bring down the network.

rubric.description: Explains star topology.
rubric.why: The central device is the defining arrangement of star topology.
rubric.how: State that nodes communicate via a central switch or hub and give its repeater role.

rubric.description: Explains ring topology.
rubric.why: The circular arrangement, direction of travel, and failure effect distinguish ring topology.
rubric.how: State that devices form a circle, data travels in one direction, and a failed connection can affect the network.

rubric.description: Explains mesh topology and its benefit.
rubric.why: The direct connections and resulting reliability distinguish mesh topology.
rubric.how: State that every device connects to every other device and that this provides alternative routes or high reliability.

written.text: Explain the Von Neumann architecture of a computer. Include a discussion on the main components, their functions, and the step-by-step process of how the architecture operates.
modelAnswer: The Von Neumann architecture is a computer model with memory, a Central Processing Unit (CPU), input devices, and output devices.
Memory contains both input data and the instructions required for CPU processing.
The CPU includes the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) and the Control Unit (CU).
The ALU performs mathematical computations and logical operations; the CU directs activities and decodes instructions.
Input devices enter data and instructions into the computer system.
Output devices present or communicate the outcomes of tasks executed by the computer.
First, the CPU fetches an instruction from memory; the CU then decodes it.
The CPU executes the instruction using the ALU and/or CU, and the result is stored in memory or sent to an output device.

written.text: Explore the different types of computing systems such as computers, software systems, computer networks, and the internet.
modelAnswer: The types of computing systems include computers, software systems, computer networks, and the Internet.
A computer is a system designed to process data and perform tasks according to instructions.
Software is a collection of instructions that dictate the requirements and actions that hardware must do.
System software manages computer resources, while application software carries out certain functions for the user.
A computer network connects multiple computers and devices, enabling the exchange of resources and information.
Networks can share files, printers, and Internet access and can enable communication and data management.

written.text: Describe in detail how integers are stored in computer memory.
modelAnswer: Computer memory stores an integer as a pattern of binary bits, each having a value of 0 or 1.
The number of bits allocated to the integer determines how many different values can be stored.
For an unsigned n-bit integer, all bit patterns represent non-negative values, from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1.
A signed integer must also represent negative values.
A common signed representation is two's complement.
To form a negative value in two's complement, write the positive value in binary, invert its bits, and add 1.
For example, in 4 bits, 5 is 0101; invert to get 1010 and add 1 to get 1011, which represents −5.
Thus, the same bit pattern is interpreted according to whether the integer is signed or unsigned.

written.text:
Explain the process of converting a decimal integer to its binary representation and vice versa. Include examples of both positive and
negative integers.
modelAnswer: To convert a positive decimal integer to binary, divide by 2 repeatedly and record each remainder.
Read the remainders from bottom to top.
For 13: 13 ÷ 2 = 6 remainder 1; 6 ÷ 2 = 3 remainder 0; 3 ÷ 2 = 1 remainder 1; 1 ÷ 2 = 0 remainder 1.
Therefore, 13₁₀ = 1101₂.
To convert binary to decimal, multiply each bit by its power-of-2 place value and add: 1101₂ = 1 × 8 + 1 × 4 + 0 × 2 + 1 × 1 = 13₁₀.
For a negative integer, use a fixed number of bits and two's complement.
In 4 bits, 5 is 0101; invert the bits to get 1010 and add 1 to get 1011.
Therefore, −5₁₀ = 1011₂ in 4-bit two's complement; conversely, 1011₂ represents −5₁₀.

written.text: Explain the systematic process of troubleshooting. Describe each step in detail.
modelAnswer: 1. Identify the problem: observe and clearly describe what is wrong.
2. Establish a theory of probable cause: suggest a likely reason for the problem.
3. Test the theory to determine the cause: check whether the suspected cause is correct.
4. Establish a plan of action to resolve the problem: decide what steps or repair are needed.
5. Implement the solution: carry out the selected plan.
6. Verify full system functionality: test that the problem is fixed and the system works properly.
7. Document findings, actions, and outcomes: record what was found, what was done, and the result.

written.text: Discuss the importance of troubleshooting in maintaining the smooth operation of systems, especially computing systems.
modelAnswer: Troubleshooting helps identify and fix problems quickly so systems operate smoothly and efficiently.
It can reduce downtime, which helps prevent lost productivity.
It can help find the source of data corruption and protect data integrity.
It can identify security vulnerabilities and help protect the system.
It can find causes of slow performance, such as insufficient memory, software conflicts, or hardware malfunctions.
Fixing small issues early can extend equipment life and save the cost of expensive repairs or replacements.
When systems work reliably, users can complete tasks efficiently and have a better experience.

written.text: Describe the process of using utility software to optimize system performance and maintain security. Provide detailed steps and examples of common utility tools.
modelAnswer: Run Disk Cleanup to scan the hard drive for temporary, cached and other unnecessary files that can safely be deleted.
Removing these files can reclaim disk space and may improve performance.
Use antivirus software to scan files and incoming data for known viruses and malware signatures.
Keep its real-time protection enabled to help prevent virus attacks.
Schedule backup software to copy files and folders to an external drive, cloud storage or a network location.
Backups allow files to be retrieved if they are accidentally deleted.
Use file compression tools to place one or more files in an archive such as ZIP.
Compression reduces file size, making files easier to store or transfer.

written.text: Explain Substitution Cipher Method with examples
modelAnswer: In a substitution cipher, each letter of the original message (plaintext) is replaced by another letter according to a key or rule.

To decrypt it, shift each letter three places backward: KHOOR becomes HELLO.

written.text: What is confidentiality of data and information?
modelAnswer: Confidentiality of data and information means protecting it from unauthorized access or disclosure.

written.text: Define phishing attack. Also write three characteristics of phishing Email and phishing website.
modelAnswer: A phishing attack is a fraudulent attempt to trick people into revealing sensitive information by pretending to be a trustworthy person or organization.
A phishing email may come from a misleading sender, use urgent language, or contain a suspicious link or attachment.
A phishing website imitates a genuine website and may use a misleading web address.
It may ask visitors to enter passwords, bank details or other personal information.

written.text: Define hub or switch.
modelAnswer: A hub or switch is a networking device used to connect computers or other devices in a LAN.
A hub sends received data to all its ports, whereas a switch forwards data to the intended device.

written.text: File sharing
modelAnswer: File sharing allows users on a computer network to access or exchange files stored on another computer.
Users can share documents, data, and other files through a shared network folder or server.
It allows several users to use the same files without making separate copies on each computer.

modelAnswer: A password is used to protect a computer, account, or information from unauthorised access.
A good password should be at least 8 characters long.
It should combine different character types, such as uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols.
It should be difficult to guess and should not use obvious personal information.

modelAnswer: A client connects to a server over the Internet using the TCP/IP protocol.

modelAnswer: Integrity means ensuring that data remains accurate and complete and is not changed without authorization.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing restricted access or disclosure.

written.text: Write a note on star topology.
modelAnswer: In a star topology, every computer or device is connected to a central hub or switch.
Each device has its own link to this central device, which manages communication.
It is easy to add a device and to identify a fault in an individual link.
If the central hub or switch fails, communication across the network may stop.

written.text: Write a note on ring topology.
modelAnswer: In a ring topology, each device is connected to two neighbouring devices, forming a closed loop.
Data passes from one device to the next around the ring.
The devices cooperate to forward data along the ring to its destination.
A failed device or broken link can disrupt communication around the network.

rubric.how: State that a device is linked to the device on either side.

modelAnswer: Unauthorized access: an unauthorised person views or uses data without permission.

modelAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices through a transmission medium.
The sender is the device that sends the data, and the receiver is the device that receives it.
The message is the data being communicated; the medium is the path through which it travels.
A protocol is the set of rules that controls how devices communicate.

A key is used to decrypt the ciphertext and recover the original information.
Encryption helps keep personal and confidential data private from people who are not authorized to read it.
It is used in everyday internet services such as online banking, online shopping, and secure messaging.

written.text: Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).
modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all devices share a single communication line called a bus.
If the main cable fails, the whole network goes down.
In a star topology, each node communicates with the others via a central switch or hub.
The hub works as a data flow repeater.
In a ring topology, each device is connected in a circular pathway with other devices.
Data travels in one direction, passing through each device; if one connection fails, the whole network is affected.
In a mesh topology, each device is connected to every other device.
This provides high redundancy and reliability because data can be rerouted through other links.

written.text:
Consider a shift cipher with a shift amount of 4.
(a) Encrypt the message "SECURITY".
(b) Decrypt the message "WMXYVMI".
modelAnswer: (a) Shift each letter of SECURITY four places down the alphabet.
S → W, E → I, C → G, U → Y, R → V, I → M, T → X, Y → C
Encrypted message = WIGYVMXC
(b) Shift each letter of WMXYVMI four places back in the alphabet.
W → S, M → I, X → T, Y → U, V → R, M → I, I → E
Decrypted message = SITURIE

written.text: Describe how data is transmitted across computer networks using packet switching and circuit switching.
modelAnswer: In packet switching, the message is divided into smaller units called packets.
Each packet carries information needed for delivery and may travel through shared network routes.
Packets can take different routes to the destination.
At the destination, the packets are put back together to form the original message.
In circuit switching, a dedicated communication path is established before data is sent.
The path remains reserved for the communication while it is in use.
Packet switching shares network capacity among packets, while circuit switching reserves a path.
Thus, the two methods differ in whether data uses shared routes or a dedicated connection.

written.text: Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).
modelAnswer: In a star topology, each device connects to a central hub or switch.
It is easy to manage, and one device or link failing usually does not stop the other devices, but the central device is a critical point.
In a ring topology, each device connects to two neighbouring devices to form a closed loop.
A break in the ring can disrupt communication unless a bypass or other protection is available.
In a bus topology, all devices share one main backbone cable.
It uses less cable, but a failure of the backbone can affect the whole network and faults may be harder to locate.
In a mesh topology, devices have multiple links or paths between them.
Mesh can be highly reliable because data may use another path, but it can require more connections and cost more.

written.text: Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).

In a ring topology, each device is connected in a circular pathway with other devices.
Data travels in one direction, passing through each device; if one connection fails, the whole network is affected.
In a mesh topology, each device is connected to every other device.

written.text: Define flow chart? Write a note on any three advantages and disadvantages of flow chart.

2. It helps in analyzing a problem and finding errors.

Disadvantages:

written.text: Pseudocode for determining if a number is prime.

Input: number {The number to be checked}
Output: True if number is prime, False otherwise

return False
end if
end for
return True
End

written.text: Discuss the concept of decomposition in computational thinking. Why is it important?
modelAnswer: Decomposition is the process of breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable parts.
Each part can be understood and solved separately, which makes the whole problem less difficult.
The parts can be tested individually and then combined to form the complete solution.
For example, planning a school event can be decomposed into arranging a venue, preparing a schedule, inviting participants, and organising equipment.
Each task can be assigned and checked separately, making the event easier to plan successfully.

written.text: Define computational thinking and explain its significance in modern problem-solving. Provide examples to illustrate how computational thinking can be applied in different fields.
modelAnswer: Computational thinking is a problem-solving process that involves a set of skills and techniques to solve complex problems in a way that can be executed by a computer.
It is significant because it helps make complicated problems manageable and supports clear, logical ways of solving them.
Its key components are decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithms.
In biology, a complex investigation can be divided into smaller tasks.
In mathematics, a student can recognise patterns in numbers, such as the pattern in square areas.
In daily life, someone planning a trip can focus on necessary details and follow a sequence of steps.

written.text: Compare and contrast continuous and discrete data. Use examples to show how each type of data might be used in a school setting, such as in measuring student performance or tracking attendance.
modelAnswer: Discrete data consist of distinct, separate values that are countable, often in whole numbers.
In a school, the number of students attending class or the number of books borrowed is discrete data.
Continuous data consists of values that can take any number within a given range, including fractions or decimals.
In a school, students' heights or the time taken to complete a test are continuous data.

written.text: Differentiate between nominal, ordinal, discrete, and continuous data. For each type, describe a suitable visualization technique and provide a specific example of how this technique can be used to represent that type of data effectively.
modelAnswer: Nominal data are labels or categories without a specific order, such as favourite colours; a bar chart can show the frequency of each colour.
Ordinal data are categories with a meaningful order, such as satisfaction ratings; an ordered bar chart can show the number of responses at each level.
Discrete data are distinct, separate values that are countable, such as the number of students absent each day; a bar chart can compare the counts.
Continuous data can take any value within a range, including fractions or decimals, such as students' heights; a histogram can show the distribution of heights.

From the 2000s onward, deep learning, natural language processing, and robotics expanded AI's capabilities.
Voice assistants were used in 2011, and ChatGPT was introduced in 2023.

written.text: Describe the steps you should take to ensure the safe operation of digital platforms and devices.

Check and adjust privacy settings, and avoid sharing personal details such as your home address, phone number, or school name.
Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) to add another layer of account security.
Avoid accessing sensitive information, such as online banking, on public Wi-Fi; use a secure, private network instead.
Be skeptical of unsolicited requests for personal information and verify the source before responding.
Regularly review account activity and respond to suspicious activity by changing your password and reporting it to the platform.
Back up important data to an external hard drive or a cloud storage service.

written.text: Discuss the different types of intellectual property rights, including copyright, trademarks, and patents.
modelAnswer: Copyright is a legal right that gives creators control over their original works, such as music, books, movies, and software.
For example, an author can decide how their book is published, shared, or adapted.
Trademarks are symbols, names, or slogans used by companies to distinguish their products or services from others.

Patents protect new inventions or processes.
They give the inventor exclusive rights to make, use, or sell the invention for a certain period.
For example, an inventor may patent a new type of smartphone to prevent others from making or selling a similar phone without permission.
Thus, copyright protects original works, trademarks distinguish products or services, and patents protect new inventions or processes.

written.text: Define and describe the concept of a system. Explain the fundamental components, objectives, environment, and methods of communication within a system.
modelAnswer: A system is an organized set of components coordinated to perform a designated function.
Every system has an objective or goal that it aims to fulfil.
Its components are its building blocks; each plays a specific role and contributes to the system's functioning.
The environment includes everything external to the system that interacts with it and can affect its operation.
Communication and interaction among components help them work together in an organized way to achieve the system's objectives.
Systems also interact with their environment through inputs and outputs.
For example, a weather monitoring system receives data from environmental sensors and provides weather status and forecasts to users.

written.text: Discuss the objectives of computer networks and provide examples of how they facilitate resource sharing and data communication.
modelAnswer: The primary objectives of computer networks are resource sharing, data communication and collaboration.
Resource sharing: Computer networks allow devices to share resources, such as printers and storage, reducing costs and improving efficiency.
Example: In an office network, multiple computers can share a single printer, reducing the need for multiple printers.
Data communication: Networks facilitate data transfer, enabling communication through emails, instant messaging, and video conferencing.
Example: Employees in different locations can collaborate through video conferencing tools like Zoom or Microsoft Teams.
Connectivity and collaboration: Networks connect devices, allowing for remote access and collaboration, improving productivity and flexibility.
Example: A team can work on a shared document in real-time using cloud-based services like Google Drive.

written.text: Describe the main characteristics of a computer as a system, including its objectives, components, and interactions among these components.
modelAnswer: A computer is a complex system designed to process data and perform tasks according to a set of instructions.
Its objective is to perform computations, process data, and execute different tasks efficiently.
Interface components include input devices such as the keyboard and mouse, and output devices such as monitors and printers.
Processing components include the CPU, RAM, storage, operating system, and application software.
Communication components include the motherboard and system bus.
The motherboard interconnects components, while the system bus transmits data between the CPU and other components.
When a user opens a file using a mouse or keyboard, the input device sends a signal to the computer.
The operating system determines the appropriate action, processing components handle the task, and an output device presents the result.

written.text: Compare and contrast the different types of network topologies (star, ring, bus, and mesh).
modelAnswer: In a bus topology, all devices share a single communication line called a bus.
If the main cable fails, the whole network goes down.
In a star topology, each node communicates with the others via a central switch or hub.
The hub works as a data flow repeater.
In a ring topology, each device is connected in a circular pathway with other devices.
Data travels in one direction, passing through each device; if one connection fails, the whole network is affected.
In a mesh topology, each device is connected to every other device.
This provides high redundancy and reliability because data can be rerouted through other links.
written.followUp: What are the advantages of using a star topology in a network?

rubric.description: Explains ring topology.

rubric.description: Explains mesh topology and its benefit.
rubric.why: The direct connections and resulting reliability distinguish mesh topology.

written.text: In a Simplex communication system, assume data is transmitted at a rate of 500 bits per second (bps). Compute the time to transmit a message if: (a) it is of 10 kilobits.
modelAnswer: 1 kilobit = 1000 bits
10 kilobits = 10 × 1000 = 10000 bits
Time = Amount of data ÷ Transmission rate
Time = 10000 ÷ 500 = 20 seconds
Answer: 20 seconds
written.followUp: In a Simplex communication system, assume data is transmitted at a rate of 500 bits per second (bps). Compute the time to transmit a message if: (a) it is of 10 kilobits.

rubric.description: Convert the message size to bits.
rubric.why: The message size must be expressed in bits to use the given transmission rate.
rubric.how: Use 1 kilobit = 1000 bits: 10 × 1000 = 10000 bits.

rubric.description: Set up and evaluate the time calculation.
rubric.why: Time is found by dividing the number of bits by the transmission rate.

rubric.description: State the final answer with its unit.
rubric.why: The final value must include the correct unit of time.
rubric.how: Write 20 seconds.
